espn-603999.headline: Both lose a fly-half; South Africa send for a lock
beats: Romain Ntamack hurt a shoulder in the 54–17 win over Fiji, and France were already without Thomas Ramos and Matthieu Jalibert. Maxime Lucu came on at fly-half against Fiji and is in pole position to start there.

South Africa lost a fly-half to a shoulder too: the uncapped 20-year-old Yaqeen Ahmed has gone home. Rassie Erasmus said he had enough backline cover and replaced him with Eben Etzebeth, a lock with 147 Tests and the team record.

France's last home game against them, on 8 November 2025, ended 17–32. Win this time and France go up to third in the world rankings, with South Africa dropping to second behind New Zealand, who sit level with them on 20 points in the Nations Championship.
Erasmus says South Africa must play much better than they did in beating Italy 66–7. France would settle for knowing who plays fly-half.

espn-604000.headline: Italy have won more Tests this year than Argentina
beats: The table says otherwise. Italy are bottom of the Nations Championship with no points, and a week ago South Africa scored nine tries past them in Turin, 66–7.
Argentina have not won in five, the latest a 42–12 beating by Ireland. Their best result since July is a 28–28 draw with Australia, at home.
Win in Genova and Italy rise to ninth in the world, above Fiji and Wales. A week later Fiji come to Udine, level with Italy on no points.
Argentina go to France after this, so on paper this is their easier afternoon. Paper has done neither side many favours in 2026.

espn-604001.headline: Wales conceded 43 in July. New Zealand keep scoring it
beats: New Zealand have scored 50, 43 and 43 in their last three games, with seven tries every time. When South Africa put 43 on Wales in July, Wales did not score at all.

Their last meeting, on 22 November 2025, with Wales at home, finished 26–52. Wales prepared for this one by edging Japan 28–21, a win Steve Tandy admitted was below par and in which captain Dewi Lake said his side had let themselves down.

New Zealand could be without Jordie Barrett and Will Jordan, both hurt at Murrayfield. That came at the end of a week Dave Rennie said left some players visibly upset at the final whistle. They still won by 22.
Louis Rees-Zammit was the bright spot against Japan, with his first try in eight internationals. A win would lift Wales to ninth in the world, above Fiji, and it would take more than one wing.

espn-604002.headline: Seven tries answered the rumours. Japan get the next say
beats: The week The Times reported that England players had lost faith in Steve Borthwick, England put seven tries past Australia, 45-22. Jamie George called the article "shocking". Then he scored the first try, his 18th in Tests, and screamed at the crowd.

Eddie Jones' Japan arrive on two straight defeats, the latest 28-21 in Cardiff, where Wales did not score the decisive try until the 69th minute. They were ninth in the world in October and are twelfth now.
A Japan win would lift them above Fiji, Wales and Italy and drop England below Scotland and Australia. Australia are the side England just beat by 23.
New Zealand come to the same ground a week later. A slip here would hand the rumours their best material yet.

espn-604003.headline: A win keeps Ireland third. Anything less costs it
beats: Fiji have lost all four Nations Championship games and conceded 54 in Lyon last Saturday, eight tries to two. Beating them earns Ireland no ranking ground, while a draw drops them below France to fourth.

Ireland scored six tries in a 42–12 win over Argentina and were wasteful in the 22 late on, so there was more to be had. They sit level on points with England in fourth but well behind on points difference, and finals weekend pairs third with fourth. Margin is the only thing on offer.
Jake White started ten France-based players in Lyon, including his entire backline, and still the backs struggled to fire. Fiji did beat Japan 34–28 in October.
South Africa come to Dublin six days later. Fiji go to Italy, the only other side yet to take a point.

espn-604004.headline: Both shipped 43 or more last week. One stops here
beats: Scotland lost 43–21 to New Zealand at Murrayfield. A day later Australia lost 45–22 to England at Twickenham, in Les Kiss's first Nations Championship game in charge. Gregor Townsend's answer was to tell his players that "no one is undroppable".

Australia's defence is the deeper worry. They conceded 50 and 43 to New Zealand in October, then England's 45, three straight losses. The one high point of their year was putting 42 on South Africa, and they needed every point of it.
Win and Scotland climb above England in the world rankings, a reward for doing to Australia what England just did, only less.

The sides have met 35 times, Australia winning 22. Townsend spent a summer playing club rugby in Sydney in the 1990s. Against Australia, his Scotland sides have produced some of the best rugby of his tenure.

espn-604005.headline: Someone other than South Africa did it last year
beats: England beat New Zealand 33–19 at home on 15 November 2025. After the 43–21 win over Scotland, a Planet Rugby column called this still an average New Zealand side that someone other than South Africa would expose eventually.

Scotland were within three points at half-time. Dave Rennie blamed first-half ill-discipline and two yellow cards, in a week when the squad's head of security died at the team hotel in Edinburgh. New Zealand then won the second half going away.

England put seven tries past Australia, 45–22. Jamie George scored the first, two days after calling reports of a rift between the players and Steve Borthwick "shocking". Win by 16 or more and England go up to third in the world, above Ireland and France.
New Zealand's defeats in September both came against South Africa. England would like to be the other side the column had in mind.

espn-604006.headline: Scotland leak 43, Japan lose by a score. One gives.
beats: Scotland have conceded 43 twice this year: to Ireland in March, and to New Zealand at Murrayfield on 7 November, with only three points between the sides at half-time.
Japan's trouble runs the other way. They lost 34–28 to Fiji and 28–21 to Wales in Cardiff, where Wales did not land the decisive score until the 69th minute and Eddie Jones's side were left "fuming".
Scotland's best attacking day was seven tries in Argentina, and they still let in 38. A Japan win of any size sends Scotland below Australia in the world rankings.
One side keeps letting points in. The other keeps running out of game to get them back.

espn-604007.headline: Ireland's scrum has had a year to think about this
beats: South Africa won 24–13 at the Aviva Stadium on 22 November 2025. Andrew Porter has not played for Ireland since last November, and has spent almost a year stewing over the scrum.

Ireland opened the window with six tries against Argentina, three of them for Hugo Keenan, and Andy Farrell still wants them more ruthless. South Africa put 66 past Italy, 45 of it before half-time, and Rassie Erasmus says "we have to play much better than this if we want to be competitive against France and Ireland."
South Africa top the Nations Championship only on points difference from New Zealand. An Irish win would also drop them to second in the world, below New Zealand.
Neither side has another game listed until the World Cup, which leaves a long time to remember a scrum.

espn-604008.headline: Nobody has won yet. Somebody has to in Udine
beats: After four rounds, Italy and Fiji are the only sides in the Nations Championship without a point. Twenty points of difference separate them, and Fiji at least remember winning this year: they beat Japan 34–28 in October.
Italy have lost five straight. The latest was 66–7 to South Africa in Turin, nine tries, all converted. Fiji were spared nothing either, beaten 54–17 by France the same day.
The stakes are oddly generous: win by any margin and Italy, bottom of the log, go up to ninth in the world, above Fiji and Wales.
After this, Italy's next Test is a World Cup game against South Africa in October 2027. That makes a long time to sit on a loss.

espn-604009.headline: France need 16 points of daylight. They usually bring it
beats: France's last three wins came by 37, 27 and 16 points. Sixteen is the line at the Stade de France: win by that much and France go above Ireland into third in the world.
Fabien Galthié has had his own problems. France put eight tries past Fiji and came out of it preparing for the Springboks without their four leading fly-halves.
Argentina spent the middle of the year losing narrowly, by seven to South Africa and to England and by six to Australia. Then Ireland scored six tries and won by 30.
Losing by seven has become an Argentina habit. France's habit lately is more than twice that.

espn-604010.headline: Australia have shipped 45, 43 and 50. Next, Cardiff
beats: England ran in seven tries past them on 8 November, Les Kiss's first Nations Championship game in charge. New Zealand had already put 50 and 43 on them in October. Australia's last win came in September, when they scored 42 against South Africa.
Wales are not obviously the side to cash in. They edged Japan 28–21 in Cardiff, and captain Dewi Lake said they had let themselves down. It was a fourth win in 13 Tests under Steve Tandy.

Before Australia, Wales host New Zealand in Cardiff. That is either preparation or a warning. A Welsh win by 16 or more would drop Australia below Argentina in the world rankings, so a defence this generous has a ranking riding on it.
After this, the next fixture on Australia's books is a World Cup game against Hong Kong in October 2027. That leaves a long time to think about tackling.
